questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver crash ahead, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely near the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely near the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what you saw about the aggressive behavior.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.
Wave your arms at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: ____ is required emergency equipment.
questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Unbalanced weight in a trailer:

options.text: Can make it hard to handle safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make it hard to handle safely.
questions.explanation: Unbalanced weight in a trailer makes it unsafe to handle. Too much or too little weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Weight should be spread evenly from front to back and side to side, and placed as low as possible.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle than yours:

options.text: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
Usually takes longer to stop than your vehicle.
Takes about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can usually stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far to stay behind other cars.

questions.question: During a pre-trip engine inspection, you should:

options.text: Put the engine in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: When checking your engine during a pre-trip inspection, start it and listen for any strange sounds.

questions.question: Compressed air often contains:
questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Tanks must be drained regularly.

questions.question: You should stop every ____ to take a break and avoid fatigue.
questions.correctAnswerText: Two hours
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on long drives, stop for a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles.

questions.question: You may be driving aggressively if you:

options.text: Slow down and keep a safe following distance.
Make hand gestures that anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, keeping safe distances, and not making gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.question: Parked delivery trucks are hazardous because:

options.text: Drivers may rush out without checking for traffic.
Packages often fall into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may rush out without checking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery or postal trucks are dangerous because drivers may pull into traffic suddenly or step out without looking for other vehicles.

questions.question: Which agency conducts threat assessments for hazardous materials endorsements?
questions.correctAnswerText: The TSA
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts threat assessments for drivers seeking a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: When turning, drivers usually look:

options.text: In the direction of the turn.
In the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Drivers naturally look in the direction they are turning. Even without a signal, body movements can show that a driver plans to turn.

questions.question: To know if a vehicle can handle a load, you need to check:

options.text: The tire rating for the front tires only.
The tire rating for the rear tires only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's suspension rating.
questions.explanation: You must know your vehicle's weight capacity and suspension system rating. It is your responsibility to make sure your vehicle is not overloaded and stays within legal weight limits.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, start by:

options.text: Turning the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turning the steering wheel opposite the direction of the turn.
Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel opposite the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite the direction you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, air pressure enters the brake chambers when the driver:
questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Pressing the brake pedal sends air into the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, check for all of the following except:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers.
questions.explanation: Check that tires have proper tread depth (at least 4/32 inch on front tires and 2/32 inch on others), are not cracked, have correct air pressure, and are all the same size. The manufacturer does not matter.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a slope.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake whenever you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Who is responsible for ensuring cargo is loaded properly?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for inspecting cargo, recognizing overloads and imbalanced weight, securing cargo without blocking the view, and ensuring cargo does not block access to emergency equipment.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly toward the floor.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times and then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another problem in the braking system.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the air brake system from too much pressure buildup. It is usually set to open at 150 psi.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil. These build up in the air storage tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these buildups. Tanks with a manual drain valve should be drained at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: When checking your tires before a trip, what should you look at?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that tire pressure is correct. It should not be too low or too high.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a vehicle fire, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the firefighters
questions.explanation: If you do not know which fire extinguisher to use on a vehicle fire, especially if it involves hazardous materials, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them put it out.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used:

options.text: To make the air brakes work more effectively
To temporarily release the spring brakes
To charge the brakes on the rear trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: To temporarily release the spring brakes
questions.explanation: A separate air tank in vehicles with dual parking control valves can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Activating the proper control releases the spring brakes for a short time, letting the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When doing a pre-drive inspection:

options.text: The inspection report is not important
The inspection report must only be reviewed if there will be passengers
You should review the previous inspection report, if there is one

questions.correctAnswerText: You should review the previous inspection report, if there is one
questions.explanation: The first step of a vehicle inspection is to review the last inspection report. Only sign the report after confirming that any noted defects have been repaired.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery right after rain starts because:

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road
Tires are not made for wet weather
Water has not yet absorbed the dirt and grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts because water creates a slick film when it mixes with oil and grease on the road surface that has not washed away yet.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill:

options.text: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking
Downshift continuously instead of using the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking
questions.explanation: On long or steep downhill grades, mainly use engine braking to control your vehicle speed. Use your brakes only to help slow down.

questions.question: In very hot weather, you should check tires regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure increases as temperature rises
The tread wears down faster than in cooler weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases as temperature rises
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature. Pay special attention to tire mounting and pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: A truck should be parked:

options.text: So that it must be backed up to leave
So that it can be pulled forward to leave

questions.correctAnswerText: So that it can be pulled forward to leave
questions.explanation: You cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Backing up is always dangerous and should be avoided. Park in spaces where you can pull forward when you leave.

questions.question: When driving, it is important to:

options.text: Avoid using your mirrors in heavy traffic
Look only at the front and right side of the vehicle
Look at the front, sides, and rear of the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the front, sides, and rear of the vehicle
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Watch the road ahead and check both side mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: What happens if brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: Some brakes work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check your brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: What are escape ramps used for?

options.text: To leave the highway and enter a two-lane road.
To safely stop vehicles that lose their brakes on steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: To safely stop vehicles that lose their brakes on steep hills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill sections of road. They have loose, soft material to stop runaway vehicles safely.

questions.question: What usually happens to bridges in freezing temperatures?

options.text: They have heaters to prevent freezing.
They freeze before other road surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular road surfaces. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, what is the minimum following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length?
questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds under 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add at least one more second.

questions.question: When should you inspect cargo during a trip?

options.text: Only at the start of the drive.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: After every break you take.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and its straps before you start driving. After you begin, check within the first 50 miles, then every 3 hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover your cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo.
To protect the cargo from bad weather.
To protect the cargo from animals.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from animals.
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather. Protecting cargo from animals is not a primary reason.

questions.question: Brakes can quickly go out of adjustment especially when:
questions.correctAnswerText: They are hot.
questions.explanation: Hot brakes go out of adjustment quickly. Check your brakes often. Properly working and adjusted brakes are needed to control your vehicle safely.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Use your taillights to warn other drivers.
Do not worry about other drivers.
Turn on your four-way emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This is especially important when it is hard to see. Place warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: When should you shift into a lower gear before going downhill?

options.text: As you go downhill and gain speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going downhill.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear and slow down before going downhill. If you start downhill too fast, your brakes may overheat and fail.

questions.question: How can you help prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens more easily if your tires are worn or your tire pressure is too low. If you start to hydroplane, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: What should you do when a worker is in a work zone?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower than the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: When workers are present in a work zone, you must drive slower than the posted speed limit to keep them safe.

questions.question: What is true about a distracted driver?

options.text: They usually follow the rules of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They notice hazards more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see hazards on the road much more slowly than focused drivers. They may miss hazards completely.

questions.question: What is a problem with retarders?
questions.correctAnswerText: They are not allowed everywhere.
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle without using brakes. However, they are noisy and not permitted in all areas.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle is hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: When hydroplaning, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: What should you check closely during a winter pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coolant and antifreeze levels
questions.explanation: In winter, pay extra attention to coolant and antifreeze levels. Also check the heating and defrosting equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer, tires, tire chains, lights, reflectors, windows, mirrors, steps, and exhaust system.

questions.question: When can you remove the radiator cap?

options.text: Not when the coolant is hot.
When the cap feels cool under normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not when the coolant is hot.
questions.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap while the system is hot. Steam and boiling water can escape and burn you severely. Wait until the cap is cool to the touch before opening it.

questions.question: Why should you see part of your vehicle in the side mirror?

options.text: It limits the view behind the trailer.
It helps you judge where nearby objects are.
It lets you see stickers on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you judge where nearby objects are.
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted side mirror shows part of your vehicle. This gives you a reference point to judge the location of objects near you.

questions.question: When should you inspect your cargo during a trip?

options.text: Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Inspect your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. Check it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: When changing lanes, should you use turn signals?

options.text: Only if a vehicle is close to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, every time.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you signal.

questions.question: What does not need to be on an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the trip origin and destination, the Vehicle Identification Number, and fuel purchased. It does not need to include how many meals the driver ate.
